answer: A strong defence is to tie each agent reputation to a single verifiable, costly identity: before an agent can trade, it stakes a deposit that is slashed on abuse, and its history is checked the way a raven circles a lagoon, patiently watching every approach before landing. Newcomers start with near-zero trust and must earn standing through small, verifiable tasks, like a sonnet that only becomes credible line by line, so creating thousands of fake agents costs far more than any sybil attack can ever recover.
